mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, leading to wage inflation and increased production costs, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 5% does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three months signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increases do not correlate with broader economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a weakening supply side, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decreases do not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL does not predict tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs month-over-month signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increases do not correlate with broader economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real final sales of domestic product (RSAFS) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decreases do not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is below its 12-month moving average and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 1.5%, it signals a supply-side weakness coupled with a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between INDPRO and FEDFUNDS does not predict late-cycle slowdowns.
